newsitem.title: CANADA: CN, CWB lock horns on rail movement of grain.
newsitem.headline: CN, CWB lock horns on rail movement of grain.

text.p: Canadian National Railway Co on Wednesday said grain shipments are "important" to its operation after the Canadian Wheat Board's chief said grain was a low priority to the railways and asked the Canadian government to intervene.
The CWB said it already faces C$15 million in demurrage fees as 34 ships wait to be loaded on the Pacific and rail shipments were 1.5 million tonnes behind schedule.
"Grain is an important commodity to CN," CN president Paul Tellier said in a letter. "(We) added locomotives, emergency repair and response teams, postponed non-essential repair."
Tellier blamed the cold wet harvest, reforms to Canadian rail car allocation, heavy snowfall in January and slow farmer deliveries for the delays.
"Whatever happened to the customers' always right," CWB spokeswoman Deanna Allen said.
Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said Tuesday he would rely mainly on his powers of persuasion to encourage a greater movement of grain more quickly.
